text:
Olivia: Heads up — seeing a regression on a subset of inference racks. Throughput down ~18% and tail latencies spiking. Looks related to cont-batching + kv cache. Memory for kvslots drifts upward on long contexts (>10k tokens).

Raj: Where did this show up? prod or canary? any flamegraphs/pprof yet?

Olivia: Prod first noticed by alerts, then reproduced on canary. Attached quick heatmap from the q2 perf job: kv-merge wait spikes when batches try to merge.

Maria: paste of perf snap (trimmed):
```
flamegraph: contbatch_merge  42%
  kv_cache_lock_wait 18%
  kv_slot_rebind   9%
  kernel_dispatch  6%
  token_gen        7%
```

Tyler: hmm. That kv_slot_rebind chunk looks like reuse/eviction churn. Are merges producing uneven batch sizes (merge-skew) so head-of-line batches block others?

Olivia: Exactly. Observed lots of small batch tails that block a big merge waiting on KV allocation, then head-of-line blocking the rest of the queue.

Sasha: I ran the repro with debug counters on contbatch. Logs show repeated split/merge around same kvslot ids: id 0x7f2a... repeatedly pinned/unpinned causing noisy eviction.

Sasha: sample log:
```
[2024-10-12T14:11:02Z] contbatch: merge try id=172, size=3
[2024-10-12T14:11:02Z] kvcache: allocate slot=512 fail -> evict slot=481 (age=1.2s)
[2024-10-12T14:11:02Z] contbatch: head-wait slot=512 merge-wait=73ms queue=28
[2024-10-12T14:11:02Z] kvcache: rebind slot=512 -> new-owner=merge-173
```

Maria: That 73ms merge-wait is the one. If merge tries to grab a fresh slot while eviction is ongoing, you get HOL blocking. Over many cycles this inflates memory & refcounts because we keep fragments pinned in 'cold' state.

Raj: Do we have telemetry for slot fragmentation (free-run lengths) and reuse distance?

Tyler: I added a quick probe: reuse-distance histogram shows a heavy peak at 0 (immediate reuse) and a tail at >10s. Means some slots are reused quickly while others stay pinned. Merge heuristics prefer coalescing by sequence length which increases locality but also collides on same slots.

Olivia: Hypothesis: current merge policy biases toward minimal depth increase, which unintentionally funnels batches that share the same kv keys into same slot ranges -> localized contention + eviction pressure.

Sasha: Tried two experiments on canary: 1) disable aggressive coalesce (contbatch.coalesce_threshold=0.2 -> 0.05) 2) add short randomized jitter to merge ordering. Results: 1) reduced merge-wait by ~40% but increased token-cost by ~3%. 2) jitter reduced hot-slot thrash but slightly increased latency variance.

Maria: Attached small script I ran to collect slot metrics (python psuedocode):
```
for slot in kvslots:
  metrics.hist('slot_age', now - slot.last_unpin)
  metrics.count('slot_rebind', slot.rebinds)
  metrics.hist('slot_fragment_len', slot.fragment_count)
```

Raj: Can we add a fallback policy: if merge-wait > X ms then split merge (force small batches) and fallback to next slot region? That might avoid HOL but affect per-token efficiency.

Tyler: We prototyped a 'merge-abort-on-slot-lock' in local dev: if kv_lock_wait > 20ms then abort merge and schedule split. Throughput improved for replays with longctxs, fewer memory drifts. Will run more stable perf runs tomorrow.

Olivia: Also observed kernel selection interplay: when the kernel switches to quantized path it increases memory pressure slightly (more pinned fragments). Might be that kernel dispatch is amplifying the effect under load. Maria can you correlate kernel type with slot churn?

Maria: On it. Preliminary shows xq8 path has 12% higher slot_rebind rate on these canaries. Could be alignment or smaller allocator buckets.

Sasha: Next steps I propose:
- roll the merge-abort-on-slot-lock to canary 2 (low-risk)
- enable contbatch.coalesce reduction flag behind feature flag
- add slot fragmentation + rebind telemetry to dashboards
- run 24h soak with longctx traces

Olivia: +1. Also add an alert on sustained slot_rebind rate > threshold for 5m.

ci-bot: perf-run triggered: run_id=perf-20241012-09 merge-abort-probe, status=queued

Raj: If perf-run confirms, we should consider a medium-term fix: smarter slot allocator that prefers scatter allocation across slot ranges for merges, or soft-reservation for KV slots during merge windows. Both will need more design.

Tyler: Agreed. I'll follow up with a design doc once the perf runs finish. For now let's get the canary probes in and the telemetry up.

Olivia: Thanks team — ping me if you see any regressions in canary. I'll monitor memory and tail latencies. :thumbsup:
